from solution import sequential_search


def test_issue_example_from_issue():
    """Example: sequential_search([11,23,58,31,56,77,43,12,65,19],31) == (True, 3)."""
    # hand count 0:11, 1:23, 2:58, 3:31 so index is 3
    assert sequential_search([11, 23, 58, 31, 56, 77, 43, 12, 65, 19], 31) == (True, 3)


def test_issue_found_at_first_position():
    """Search must find element at the first position with index 0."""
    # hand count 0:7 only, so index is 0
    assert sequential_search([7, 14, 21, 28], 7) == (True, 0)


def test_issue_found_at_last_position():
    """Search must find element at the last position of the list."""
    # hand count 0:7, 1:14, 2:21, 3:28 so index is 3
    assert sequential_search([7, 14, 21, 28], 28) == (True, 3)


def test_issue_single_element_found():
    """Search in single-element list must return (True, 0) when present."""
    # hand count 0:42 so index is 0
    assert sequential_search([42], 42) == (True, 0)


def test_issue_absent_item_reports_false():
    """Search for absent element must report False flag."""
    # 99 is not in list, so flag must be False literal
    result = sequential_search([4, 6, 8, 10], 99)
    assert result[0] is False


def test_issue_empty_list_reports_false():
    """Search in empty list must report False flag."""
    # empty list contains nothing, so flag must be False literal
    result = sequential_search([], 10)
    assert result[0] is False


def test_issue_duplicate_returns_first_index():
    """Sequential search must return first occurrence index for duplicates."""
    # hand count 0:5, 1:7, 2:5, 3:9 so first 5 is at index 0
    assert sequential_search([5, 7, 5, 9], 5) == (True, 0)


def test_issue_negative_value_found():
    """Search must find negative value by equality."""
    # hand count 0:-3, 1:-1, 2:0, 3:2 so -1 is at index 1
    assert sequential_search([-3, -1, 0, 2], -1) == (True, 1)


def test_issue_string_value_found():
    """Search must find string element by equality."""
    # hand count 0:apple, 1:banana, 2:cherry so cherry is at index 2
    assert sequential_search(["apple", "banana", "cherry"], "cherry") == (True, 2)


def test_contract_found_result_is_two_tuple():
    """Found result must be a 2-tuple as in example (True, index)."""
    # hand count 0:10, 1:20 so 20 is at index 1; length literal is 2
    result = sequential_search([10, 20], 20)
    assert isinstance(result, tuple) and len(result) == 2


def test_contract_found_flag_is_bool_true():
    """Found flag must be boolean True, not just truthy."""
    # hand count 0:1, 1:2, 2:3 so 2 is at index 1
    result = sequential_search([1, 2, 3], 2)
    assert result[0] is True


def test_contract_input_list_not_modified():
    """Search must not modify the given list."""
    # original literal list [9, 4, 6] must stay equal after search
    data = [9, 4, 6]
    sequential_search(data, 4)
    assert data == [9, 4, 6]
